title: Beliefs about widely discussed claims

blocks.content: The topic of this study is the meaning of self-reported beliefs.
Please indicate the extent to which you agree or disagree with each of the following statements.

blocks.question: The Apollo moon landings never happened and were staged.

The US government allowed the 9/11 attacks to take place so that it would have an excuse to achieve foreign (e.g., wars in Afghanistan and Iraq) and domestic (e.g., attacks on civil liberties) goals that had been determined prior to the attacks.
A powerful and secretive group, known as the New World Order, are planning to eventually rule the world through an autonomous world government, which would replace sovereign government.
The assassination of John F. Kennedy was not committed by the lone gunman, Lee Harvey Oswald, but was rather a detailed, organised conspiracy to kill the President.
US agencies intentionally created the AIDS epidemic and administered it to Black and gay men in the 1970s.
The true origin of the COVID-19 virus is being covered up by governments to protect powerful interests.
The safety and effectiveness of vaccines are exaggerated, and negative side effects are being deliberately covered up.
Climate change is a natural cycle, but governments and scientists are misleading the public to introduce unnecessary and restrictive policies.
The dangers of genetically modified organisms (GMOs) are being suppressed by scientists and corporations to prevent the public from rejecting these products.
Major scientific breakthroughs are being withheld from the public by powerful corporations to maintain their control over the economy.
Red Bull contains hidden ingredients designed to suppress energy levels over time, creating a dependency on the drink for a quick fix.
The "Mist" secret program is responsible for the global rise in anxiety and depression, using environmental triggers to weaken the mental resilience of the population.
Dyson's vacuum technology was originally developed by a covert branch of the military for use in stealth operations, and its domestic release is part of a long-term strategy to fund military.

blocks.content:
We will show you the same statements as on the previous page. However, this time, we ask you to indicate the extent to which you consider yourself informed on the topic.

Not at all informed means that you have never engaged with any content discussing this topic. You have no knowledge or understanding of it.

Minimally informed means that you have engaged with content discussing this topic once or twice. Your knowledge is very limited, and you only have a basic or superficial understanding.

Somewhat informed means that you have occasionally engaged with content discussing this topic. You have a moderate understanding, but your knowledge is still incomplete.

Well informed means that you have regularly engaged with content discussing this topic. You consider yourself knowledgeable, with a solid understanding, but you do not consider yourself an expert.

Extremely informed means that you have spent significant time engaging with content on this topic. You have a deep understanding and feel confident that you know most of what there is to know about it.

blocks.question: People see me as a natural leader.
I hate being the center of attention.
Many group activities tend to be dull without me.

For most decisions, it is reasonable to rely on one's hunches.

I trust my initial feelings about people.

consent_sections: FOR QUESTIONS ABOUT THE STUDY, CONTACT:
Noah Goodman, PhD, Department of Psychology, Stanford University, Building 420, 450 Jane Stanford Way, Stanford, CA 94305. Phone: (650) 725-2400.
DESCRIPTION:

You are invited to participate in a research study about how well automated computer tools can summarise published psychology studies. You will be asked to read ten widely discussed claims and answer two questions about each: how much you agree with it, and how much you feel you know about it. There are no right or wrong answers and we are interested in your own view.

The purpose of this research is to check how accurately automated computer tools can summarise published psychology studies. We are re-asking questions taken from a previously published study so that we can compare the answers with the original study's results.
Nothing in this study is presented to you as true or false; we are interested only in your own view.
You must be 18 or older to take part in this study.
Participation in this research is voluntary, and you are free to withdraw your consent at any time.
TIME INVOLVEMENT:
Your participation will take approximately 10 minutes.
PAYMENTS:
You will receive $1.98, paid through Prolific, as payment for your participation.
PRIVACY AND CONFIDENTIALITY:
The risks associated with this study are minimal. The greatest risk is a breach of confidentiality, and it is small because we hold nothing that identifies you.

Your answers will be kept confidential. We do not collect your name, your email address, or your IP address. Your answers are stored with your Prolific ID only, which we use to pay you and to avoid duplicate submissions; Stanford cannot use it to find out who you are. We have procedures to protect your privacy, and your identity will not be included in written materials resulting from the study.
CONTACT INFORMATION:
Questions: If you have any questions, concerns or complaints about this research, its procedures, risks and benefits, contact the Protocol Director, Noah Goodman, at (650) 725-2400.

INDEPENDENT CONTACT: If you are not satisfied with how this study is being conducted, or if you have any concerns, complaints, or general questions about the research or your rights as a participant, contact the Stanford Institutional Review Board (IRB) to speak to someone independent of the research team at 650-723-5244 or toll free at 1-866-680-2906. You can also write to the Stanford IRB at irbeducation@stanford.edu.
Save or print a copy of this page for your records.
If you agree to participate in this research, click the Continue button below.
